name: Ratnagiri
note: 1872 census returned 99.7% of Hindus as 'Śaiva'; Smārta Shenvis under the Kavaḷe svāmī.

name: Thana
note: Places volume XIV (1882) read for the maṭha layer.

name: Kanara
note: Śṛṅgeri's stronghold: 32–39% of Hindus in castes asserted Smārta; about 45 caste entries name 'the Smart monastery at Shringeri'. No Śṛṅgeri maṭh located in the district. Rivals: the Konkan Kuṇbīs left a Liṅgāyat guide of Chitaldurg for Śṛṅgeri in 1881.

name: Nasik
note: Panchavati: tomb and monastery of a Śaṅkarācārya 'said to have come from Shringeri' (1883, pp. 518–19); Dr Kurtakoti, Śaṅkarācārya of Karvīr, lived here (1977). A Śṛṅgeri maṭh building at Nasik appears in a 1940 Mysore file.

name: Ahmadnagar
note: 'the decrees of Shankaracharya at Shankeshvar' are final; Kuṇbīs 'cannot tell whether they are Smarts or Bhagvats'.

name: Poona
note: Brahmans' pontiff the head of Śṛṅgeri; c. 1750 a Śaṅkarācārya allowed a Jain temple in the city (Places, 1885).

name: Sholapur
note: Arya Kshatris hold sanads from 'the Shankaracharya of Shringeri'; Komaṭis under Bhāskarācārya, 'deputy of Shankaracharya'.

name: Belgaum
note: Places volume describes the Saṅkeśvar maṭh in full (1884, pp. 600–02).

name: Dharwar
note: Marāṭhās, Komṭis and Khatrīs under the Śaṅkarācārya; about 7.6% of Hindus in castes asserted Smārta. A village named Shringeri near Hangal is unrelated (an old weir). Eleven of its taluks held Kudli maṭh property (1934); Bombay levied Rs 2,745 nazarana on the maṭh's Dharwar ināms (1936).

name: Bijapur
note: Marāṭhās 'Smārts … their guide being Shankarāchārya'. Six taluks held Kudli maṭh property (1934); Rs 1,167 nazarana on its Bijapur ināms (1936).

name: Kolhapur
note: Saṅkeśvar Svāmī's maṭh in the city (1886); became the Karvīr Pīṭha c. 1909 (1959, p. 874); Ambābāī temple spire added by a Śaṅkarācārya of Saṅkeśvar.

name: Surat
note: Gujarat: Vaiṣṇava (Vallabha, Svāminārāyaṇa).

name: Kathiawar
note: Its Dwarka entry (1884) describes the temple only, no maṭha.

name: Bombay
note: 1,947 Gosāvīs in 1881.

name: Bellary
note: Hampi lies in this district. Thurston: the Śṛṅgeri Svāmī's 1888 visit led to a procession dispute with Liṅgāyats.

name: Chingleput
note: The exception in the Tamil division: 60% Aiyaṅgār, 12% Smārta (1891). Crole's Manual (1879) is the descriptive source.

name: Cuddapah
note: Puṣpagiri lies in this district.

name: Kistna
note: Census shows movement in the Śaiva/Vaiṣṇava balance 1871–1891.

name: Madura
note: 42% Smārta, 26% Aiyaṅgār among Brahmans (1891); revised volume (1960) still names no seat. A Śṛṅgeri branch maṭh at Madura (Mysore files).

name: Malabar
note: 'Smarta' mostly the Nambūtiri caste judge; a madam near Tanur ascribed to Śaṅkara (1908).

name: Salem
note: Śṛṅgeri Matam's 'papal bulls' for the Marka Brahmans of Tali (1918).

name: South Canara
note: Śṛṅgeri the guru seat of non-Brahmin castes (Kharvis, Marāṭhās, Servegāras, Ares, Chaptegāras) in Thurston; gone by 1973. Rivals: the Mādhvas of Uḍupi; by 1973 Tulu Brahmans are 'largely followers of Madhvacharya'.

name: Tanjore
note: 64% of Brahmans in Smārta sub-castes (1891).

name: Travancore
note: Princely state.

name: Vizagapatam
note: Carmichael's Manual (1869) on the Smārta line 'at Sringagiri'.

name: Trichinopoly
note: About 55% Smārta among Brahmans (1891).

name: Tinnevelly
note: About 55% Smārta among Brahmans (1891).

name: Pudukota
note: Princely state.

name: Saharanpur
note: Includes Hardwar and Kankhal (Bhola Gir's Gosāins, the Nirañjanī and Nirbānī akhāṛās).

name: Meerut
note: 5,326 Gosāins (1872), 5,083 Daśanāmīs (1891).

name: Muttra
note: Rivals: Vallabha and Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava centre. Its 17,131 'Gosains' in 1891 are almost all unspecified, i.e. Vaiṣṇava gosvāmīs, not Daśanāmīs.

name: Bareilly
note: 6,169 Gosāins (1872), 4,023 Daśanāmīs (1891).

name: Moradabad
note: Salempur Gosāin maṭh (Ban mahants, 36 villages).

name: Allahabad
note: Akhāṛās at Daraganj lead the Magh/Kumbh procession.

name: Benares
note: Nirañjanī, Jūnā and Nirbānī akhāṛās; a Śṛṅgeri branch maṭh appears in a 1935 Mysore file. Rivals: Nevill (1909, pp. 92–93): 'Vedantism … almost exclusively prevails'; Rāmānanda's and Vallabha's influence is strong, 'but … the shrines dedicated to the cult of Shiva greatly predominate'. 1891 census: 4,106 Gosāins (1,899 Daśanāmī), 419 Jogīs, 141 Bairāgīs; 89.4% Hindu, 10.3% Muslim (1901).

name: Mirzapur
note: Mahant Anand Gir's 39 villages; Gosāins owned 44,784 acres.

name: Gorakhpur
note: Ram Ratangir's 36 villages; 13,944 Atīths; the Nāth temple. Rivals: the Gorakhnāth temple is the centre of the Nāth Jogīs, the rival Śaiva ascetic network.

name: Kumaun
note: 8,860 Gosāins (1872); Pinnath Gosāin colony.

name: Garhwal
note: Jyotirmaṭh and Badrinath lie here.

name: Sitapur
note: Goshains 'before the abolition of zamindari some of them were zamindars' (revised).

name: Fyzabad
note: Ayodhyā dominated by the Bairāgī akhāṛās. Rivals: the gazetteer describes Bairāgī dominance, yet the 1891 census returns 5,371 Daśanāmīs against 2,017 Bairāgīs; enumerators used these words loosely.

name: Gonda
note: Goshains 'followers of Shankaracharya'; 11,478 Daśanāmīs (1891).

name: Calcutta
note: Rivals: almost no Daśanāmīs (3 Atīths, 13 Gosāins in 1901). The ground belonged to Chaitanya Vaiṣṇavism and Kālī (Kālīghāṭ), and among the educated to the Brahmos (24 Parganas 1914).

name: Gaya
note: Bodh Gayā lies here; zamindari of the mahants 'have now lapsed' (1957). A Śṛṅgeri maṭh building at Gaya (Mysore files, 1940s).

name: Saran
note: Largest Daśanāmī circle on the map: 18,612 Atīths (1872), 26,753 (1901); absent from the revised volume.

name: Monghyr
note: Mahants of Dularpur and Suja; 1,780 in 'religious services' (1951).

name: Bhagalpur
note: Sultanganj convent of Sannyāsīs.

name: Palamau
note: Athiths still described in the revised volume.

name: Hill Tippera
note: Princely state.

name: Hooghly
note: Tārakeśvar lies here.

name: Howrah
note: Bhot-Bagān, 'the seat of the Dasanami sect in the district'; a 'Sankar Math' at Ramrajatala (1919).

name: Puri
note: Govardhana maṭha: absent in Hunter (1877), 'the Sankaracharya' maṭh in 1908, named Gobardhana in 1977. Rivals: the 70-odd maṭhs of Purī are mostly Vaiṣṇava foundations (Emār, Rāghavadāsa and others).

name: Hissar
note: Puri guru at Kharak, Giri guru at Bilak; 1,479 Gusains (1881), 2,318 Gosains (1891).

name: Karnal
note: Gosain pujaris of Shiva temples; later 'Jogis … of the Kanphara clan'. Rivals: Nāth Jogīs replace the Gosāin temple priests.

name: Kangra
district: Kangra; Kullu; Lahaul and Spiti; Hamirpur
note: Kangra Gosāin traders and lenders.

name: Jubbulpore
note: Bheraghat, held by Puri Gosāin mahants under a Bhonsla grant; 2,080 Gosāins (1891).

name: Narsinghpur
note: Sankal: a village said to take its name from Śaṅkara's stay.

name: Wardha
note: The Śṛṅgeri Śaṅkarācārya visited Nagpur c. 1903–04 (Wardha 1906).

name: Nagpur
note: Gosāins held 50–70 villages; 2,914 Gosāins (1891).

name: Raipur
note: Dharampuri estate (40 villages by 1909); Deopur Nāgā Gosāins; 3,194 Gosāins (1891).

name: Bastar
note: Feudatory state.

name: Kanker
note: Feudatory state.

name: Nandgaon
note: Feudatory state.

note: Feudatory state.

note: Feudatory state.

note: Feudatory state.

note: Feudatory state.

note: Feudatory state.

note: Feudatory state.

name: Bamra
note: Feudatory state.

name: Rairakhol
note: Feudatory state.

name: Sonpur
note: Feudatory state.

name: Kalahandi
note: Feudatory state.

name: Makrai
note: Feudatory state.

name: Akola
note: Berar: village priests 'more frequently Gosains than Brahmans'; a Brahman 'shankaracharya' office at Basim.

name: Amraoti
note: Berar.

name: Śṛṅgeri
variants: Sringeri; Shringeri; Sringéri; Srngeri; Sringagiri; Sringa-giri; Rishya-Sringa-giri; Sringiri; Shringori
note: Seat of the Jagadguru, 'proprietor of the surrounding tract'; jāgīr of about 9,144 people granted 1346; revenue c. Rs 50,000 plus Rs 1,000 a month from Mysore (Rice 1876, 1897). Located in no Bombay or Madras Places chapter. Rivals: Liṅgāyats (Kanara's Konkan Kuṇbīs left 'the Lingayat guide of Chitaldurg' for Śṛṅgeri in 1881; Bellary procession dispute 1888; Liṅgāyat conches allowed in Śṛṅgeri's processions); Mādhvas (Uḍupi; Uttarādi and Ahobila complaints 1906–07; Srirangapatna 1895; Vyāsarāja's claim to equal honours 1931); the Havig gurus (Svarṇavallī, Rāmacandrapura); and the seats that separated from it, Saṅkeśvar and Kudli, which held the Bombay Karnatak estates.

name: Saṅkeśvar
note: Seat of the Saṅkeśvar Svāmī: 30 inām villages in seven jurisdictions, Rs 30,000 a year; told as a secession from Śṛṅgeri c. 1570 (Belgaum 1884, pp. 600–02). Its villages lie mainly in Kolhapur, Belgaum and the Maratha states; those of its neighbour Kudli (Kudalgi), the first maṭh of its origin story, lie mainly in Dharwar and Bijapur (30 taluks and states in the 1934 list; 'Kudli estates' filter). A Bombay officer (1896) recommended exempting the Kudalgi Svāmī from the Arms Act like his 'brother Swami of Sankeshwar … in no way superior in position'.

name: Kudli
variants: Kudali; Kūḍali; Kudalgi; Kudli Sringeri Matt; Uddughatti Mutt
note: Confluence of the Tunga and Bhadra. A Smārta maṭh whose guru was appointed by Śṛṅgeri (Rice) or founded by the Saṅkeśvar secessionist (Belgaum). Mysore files: 'a separate branch … at the Partition of A. D. 1656-57'; income Rs 35,047 (1933), of which villages and lands outside Mysore brought Rs 16,798 and those inside Rs 5,594. Estates (Agent's list, March 1934): Dharwar (Ranibennur, Karajgi, Hangal, Kod, Shiggaon, Navalgund, Kalghatgi, Dharwar, Hubli, Ron, Gadag); Bijapur (Badami, Bagalkot, Bagevadi, Bijapur, Sindgi, Hungund); Belgaum (Parasgad); North Kanara (Mundgod); Bellary (Kudligi, Harapanahalli); Anantapur (Madakasira); Kolhapur (Torgal), Ramdurg, Sangli (Shirahatti), Miraj Senior (Lakshmeshwar), Miraj Junior (Gudageri), Savanur, Sirasangi, Jamkhandi (Kundgol). Bombay levied nazarana on the Dharwar and Bijapur ināms (Rs 2,745 and Rs 1,167, 1936) and calls the maṭh 'Kudalgi' or the 'Uddughatti Mutt'. Use the 'Kudli estates' filter to see them. Also a Mādhva maṭh (Akṣobhya Tīrtha).

name: Dvārkā
variants: Dwarka; Dwarika; Dwárka; Sharada Pith; Shārada Pīth
note: 'Shārada Pīth … endowed by the Gaekwar of Baroda, who sanctions the appointment of every new pontiff' (Gujarat 1901, p. 542).

name: Jyotirmaṭh
note: Named in lists of the four maṭhs; 'established the Joshimath monastery' (Garhwal 1910). Place entries describe only the Badrinath Rawal's winter seat.

name: Badrinath
note: Temple 'said to have been erected … by Sankara Acharya'; Nambūri Rawal from Malabar; estates of 164 villages and parts of 111 (1910).

name: Kumbakoṇam
note: 'the math of Sankaracharya', income nearly Rs 14,000, appoints the managers of three temples incl. one at Conjeeveram (Tanjore 1906). Catalogued as 'Kanchi Komakoti matt at Kumbakonam' in 1925.

name: Kāñcī
note: Where Śaṅkara 'founded a matam' (Crole 1879, p. 26); a temple managed from Kumbakoṇam (1906); the maṭh is 'of Conjeevaram' by 1936.

name: Purī (Govardhana maṭha)
note: Absent in 1877; 'the Sankaracharya' maṭh with c. 1,200 MSS (1908); 'Gobardhana Matha … still extant' (1977). A Kāñcī Kāmakoṭi ashram founded at Purī in 1973.

name: Śivagaṅgā
note: Maṭh in financial difficulty, endowments under Muzrai management at the guru's wish (Rice 1897); funds lent for the Śṛṅgeri Jagadguru's visit (1927).

name: Avani
note: 'A guru of the Smarta sect resides here' (Rice 1876, 1897); a Śaṅkarācārya temple with a State grant (1930); 'Avani Sringeri Mutt' (1933).

name: Hampi
variants: Virupaksha; Virūpākṣa; Pampa; Pampapati; Hampi Samsthanam
note: Sri Sankaracharya Virupaksha Samsthanam: its Svāmī calls it 'a branch of Sri Sringeri Mutt', papers 'left behind in the Nizam's Dominions' (Mysore file, 1935–36). No maṭh in the Bellary volumes.

name: Puṣpagiri
note: Temple hill and hamlet of Kotlur in the Cuddapah volumes; no maṭh described, and no archival file found.

name: Khidrapur
note: 'an alienated village belonging to Sankeshvar Svami' (Kolhapur 1886, p. 302).

name: Hallur
note: Rangnath temple rebuilt by the Kudalgi Svāmī, who was granted the village (Dharwar 1884, p. 722).

name: Hubli
note: Kudalgi Svāmī's crosswise-palkhi privilege upheld up to the Privy Council (Dharwar 1884, p. 757); Hubli taluk is in the Kudli maṭh's 1934 property list. (The 1923 'Hubli Sringeri Matt' file is really about Kudli.)

name: Nirmal
note: Reputed samādhi of a Śaṅkarācārya; temple of Shankaracharya Svāmī built after 1739, Government grant Rs 421 (Thana 1882).

name: Sonda
variants: Sonda; Sunda; Swadi; Svarnavalli; Honalli Math
note: Honalli (Svarṇavallī) Smārta maṭh, seat of the Havig Brahmans' guru: a separate line, not a Śṛṅgeri branch (Kanara 1883).

name: Bodh Gayā
variants: Bodh Gaya; Buddh Gaya; Budh Gaya
note: Giri maṭh, 'one of the seven Saivite orders established by Sankara Acharya' (Gaya 1906); Mahabodhi dispute.

name: Tārakeśvar
note: Mahant 'a celibate of the Dasnami order'; a public endowment after 1924; 'governed by the Sankaracharya school of thought' (1972).

name: Bhot-Bagān
note: Tashi Lama's grant to Puran Gir Gosāin (1785); mahant elected 'by the other Dasnami Mahants of Bengal' (1905).

name: Hardwar
note: Kumbh melā; Kankhal Gosāins (Bhola Gir, 4,024 acres); a Śṛṅgeri maṭh building at Haridwar (Mysore file, 1944). Rivals: the Gosāin–Bairāgī battle at Hardwar, 1760; precedence among Daśanāmī, Bairāgī and Udāsī akhāṛās at the Kumbh.

name: Bodhan
note: One of four monasteries of Bhāskarācārya, the Komaṭis' 'deputy of Shankaracharya' (Sholapur 1884).

name: Nander
note: Another of Bhāskarācārya's monasteries (Sholapur 1884).

name: Khanapur
note: 'The Smart svami has a monastery at Khanapur', with two villages: the Shenvi Smārta svāmī (Belgaum 1884, p. 91).

name: Kollur
note: Mūkāmbikā temple; image said to have been consecrated by Śaṅkara (South Kanara 1973).

name: Karkal
note: An image 'installed at Karkal by Shree Jagadguru Narasimha Bharati Swamiji of Sringeri Matha' (1973).

name: Kaladi
note: Śaṅkara's birthplace (Atkinson spells it 'Kallady'); the Śṛṅgeri Jagadguru's escort from Mysore to Kaladi (1923).

name: Rāmeśvaram
note: A Śṛṅgeri branch maṭh, named in a 1935 Mysore file on legacies.

name: Tirupati
note: Śṛṅgeri maṭh branch at Tirupati, managed by committees (1940).

name: Bangalore (Sultanpet)
note: 'Sringeri Matt, Sultanpet, Bangalore city' (1923); the Jagadguru's processions in the city (1907).

name: Mysore
note: Capital of the princely state whose Muzrai files record the Śṛṅgeri and Kudli maṭhs.

name: Sangli
note: Kudli Śṛṅgeri maṭh properties in Sangli State (1935).

name: Hole Narsipur
note: The Śṛṅgeri Svāmī's visits (1892) and an adda-palakki dispute in front of the Uttarādi maṭh (1906).

name: Srirangapatna
note: Visits of the Śṛṅgeri Svāmī to the Ranganātha temple (1894–95, 1907).

name: Nanjangud
note: The Śṛṅgeri Jagadguru's endowments to the Śrīkaṇṭheśvara temple (1892, 1907).

name: Kigga
note: Ṛṣyaśṛṅga temple, in the Śṛṅgeri jāgīr.

name: Belavadi
note: An inām village of the Śṛṅgeri maṭh (tank, quarry, land disposals 1902–40).

name: Ayodhyā
note: Dominated by the Bairāgī akhāṛās; the Gosāins appear only in the story of their expulsion from Hanumāngaṛhī. The Rāmānandī Bairāgīs were the Daśanāmīs' direct rival in the north.

name: Gokarn
note: Pilgrimage centre of Kanara castes; earlier seat of the Havig gurus' line before Sonda.

name: Udagatti
note: Where the Kudli svāmīs lived in the Bombay country; Bombay records call the maṭh 'Kudalgi' or the 'Uddughatti Mutt' (Mysore files, 1936).

name: Tīrthamuttūr
note: 'a vassal Mutt to the Sringeri Mutt, paying an annual subsidy of Rs 31-4-0'; its svāmīs consecrated at Śṛṅgeri (1923).

name: Uḍupi
note: Rival centre: seat of the Mādhva maṭhs; Kanara and South Canara Vaiṣṇava Brahmans' guru is 'a Tulu Brahman, who lives in celibacy at the Vaishnav monastery at Udipi'.
